main.description: Debugging aid: make one raw MCP request to an org-configured server as the caller, and return the server's result or the error exactly as pear saw it. Unlike the gateway's normal paths, a failure is reported in the output (with a 200) rather than as an XRPC error, so callers can show what the server actually said. Requires service-auth. Callable by any org member, who can only reach servers they are connected to.

org.description: DID of the community the server belongs to.

id.description: The server's id, as in network.habitat.mcp.defs#server.

name.description: The tool to call, for tools/call.

arguments.description: The tool's arguments as JSON text (an object), for tools/call. Text rather than a nested object so the exact JSON the caller typed reaches the server, floats included, which the atproto data model can't carry.

uri.description: The resource to read, for resources/read.

ok.description: Whether the server answered the request without an error.

durationMs.description: How long the request took, including connecting.

result.description: The server's result as pretty-printed JSON text, when ok. Text rather than a nested object for the same reason as the input's arguments.

error.description: The raw error, when not ok: a JSON-RPC error from the server, an HTTP failure, or why pear couldn't connect.

errorKind.description: Where the failure happened. not_connected: the caller has no usable connection. protocol: the server answered with a JSON-RPC error. transport: connecting or the HTTP exchange failed. invalid_response: the server's reply didn't validate against the MCP schema (for example invalid structuredContent).
